findings: Anteroposterior projection of the abdomen demonstrating a double-contrast barium enema study
Dense barium coating outlines the entire large bowel from rectum to the visualised hepatic and splenic flexures and transverse colon
The colonic mucosa of the transverse colon shows prominent haustral folds with a regular, scalloped inner contour
The ascending and descending colon appear foreshortened and smooth-walled with dense barium filling
The rectum and sigmoid colon show pooled barium in the pelvis with a rounded rectal contour
No discrete mucosal polyp, filling defect, apple-core lesion, or frank perforation is identified on this single projection
The lumbar spine shows multilevel disc-space narrowing and osteophytosis consistent with degenerative change
Pelvic bones are intact; a small rounded opacity is projected over the pubic symphysis, likely a urinary bladder calculus or phlebolith
The sigmoid and descending colon appear to converge toward the left pelvis without redundancy suggestive of sigmoid volvulus on this view
The central abdomen shows no gross small-bowel dilation or free air
differential: Normal double-contrast barium enema examination (no definite mucosal abnormality identified on this projection)
Inflammatory bowel disease (e.g., ulcerative colitis or Crohn colitis) — mucosal granularity in the transverse colon warrants further evaluation
Colonic polyps or early neoplasm — incomplete coating or overlapping loops in the sigmoid could obscure small lesions requiring additional projections
anatomyConcerns: The splenic flexure extends superiorly beyond the upper image margin, potentially excluding evaluation of the proximal transverse/splenic flexure region
Overlapping barium pools in the pelvis limit assessment of the rectosigmoid junction; additional oblique or lateral views would be standard
The small rounded pelvic midline opacity requires correlation to exclude a vesical calculus versus artifact or phlebolith
